newsitem.title: USA: Consumers sees Palisades back on line Mon.
newsitem.headline: Consumers sees Palisades back on line Mon.

text.p: Consumers Energy said Monday it expects its 780 megawatt (MW) Palisades nuclear power plant to come back on line later today and is likely to resume full power production in three to four days.
The plant, in South Haven, Mich., was shut Sunday for electrical repairs.
"We shut the plant Sunday for repairs. We discovered a disconnected wire in the isophase," said an onsite plant spokesman.
The wiring connects the unit's main generator and transformer.
"The turbine should roll on line today. It'll take three to four days before coming back to full power," he said.
The Palisades nuclear plant produces 18 percent of the Consumers Energy's total electricity output.
In the upper Midwest, temperatures were forecast to run normal to below normal through mid-week. Temperatures are forecast to drop 20-25 degrees Fahrenheit below normal Thursday.
Consumers Power, a subsidiary of CMS Energy Corp, changed its name from Consumers Power on January 1, 1997.
